items.claim: The video shows a real-life police pursuit of a person in a pickle costume.
items.justification: The video is not a real-life scene, as evidenced by the presence of a Sora AI watermark, which identifies it as content generated by OpenAI's text-to-video tool. Furthermore, there are no news reports confirming such a pursuit occurred, and the content appears to be inspired by a 'Rick and Morty' cartoon episode. Claims that the video depicts an ICE-led immigration raid are also explicitly identified as false.

evidence.statement: The video of the police pursuit of a person in a pickle costume is not a real-life scene.
evidence.support_span: Does a video of a police pursuit of a person in a pickle costume show a real-life scene? No, that's not true

evidence.statement: The video contains a watermark from Sora, an AI video generation tool from OpenAI.
evidence.support_span: The pickle video bears the watermark of Sora, an app from Open AI that generates videos from text prompts. ... Throughout the duration of the original clip, the logo of Sora -- an AI video creation tool -- was visible in a watermark on the top part of the screen and on the right.

evidence.statement: There are no news reports confirming that such a police pursuit actually occurred.
evidence.support_span: No news organizations reported that such a pursuit took place. ... A search across news resources on Google did not show any reports describing the scene as real.

evidence.statement: The video content appears to be inspired by the 'Rick and Morty' cartoon character who turns into a pickle.
evidence.support_span: The appearance of the character trying to escape from law enforcement in the video reviewed in this fact check seems to have been inspired by the third episode of the third season of the "Rick and Morty" cartoon in which one of the main characters, Rick, turns himself into a pickle

evidence.statement: Social media claims that the video depicted an immigration raid led by ICE are false.
evidence.support_span: Some claimed on social media that the scene was an immigration raid involving the police and led by ICE, but none of that was true.

items.claim: The video shows an industrial park explosion in Ezeiza, Argentina.
items.justification: The evidence confirms that the video depicts an explosion at an industrial park in Ezeiza, Argentina, occurring on November 14, 2025. Reports from AFP and satellite imagery match the footage to the Sinteplast facility, noting that the incident caused minor injuries to over 20 people. While the video has been mischaracterized on social media as an Iranian attack, the evidence identifies the location and event as an industrial explosion in Argentina.

evidence.statement: An AFP report confirmed that a fire was ignited by powerful explosions at an industrial park in Ezeiza.
The incident at the industrial park resulted in more than 20 people suffering minor injuries.
evidence.support_span: More than 20 people suffered minor injuries in the incident.

evidence.statement: The footage matches satellite imagery of the Sinteplast facility, and reports indicate the video shows Sinteplast employees running from the blast.
evidence.support_span: The report says the video shows Sinteplast employees running from the blast, and the footage matches satellite imagery of the Sinteplast facility available on Google Maps

raw_dropped: The video being shared on social media as an Iranian attack was actually filmed in Argentina in November 2025.
A Portuguese-language post identified the footage as a huge explosion in Ezeiza, a municipality near Buenos Aires.
An AFP report confirmed that a fire was ignited by powerful explosions at an industrial park in Ezeiza on November 14, 2025.

items.claim: The video shows huge numbers of crows storming an area in Tel Aviv, Israel.
items.justification: The evidence indicates that the claim linking the video to Tel Aviv, Israel, is misleading. Multiple sources, including a Fox Weather report and social media posts from as early as January 2024, identify the footage as showing great-tailed grackles swarming a parking lot in Texas, USA. The video has been circulating online for months with different geographic attributions, but the consistent identification of the birds and location points to Texas rather than Israel.

evidence.statement: The video showing large flocks of crows flying over cars is being shared with the misleading claim that it is a recent scene from Tel Aviv, Israel.
evidence.support_span: A video showing large flocks of crows flying over a few cars is being shared online with a misleading claim that it captures a recent scene from Israeli city Tel Aviv.

evidence.statement: The video has been available online since at least January 2024.
evidence.support_span: We found that the video has been available online since January 2024

evidence.statement: Earlier posts of the same video identified the location as Texas in the United States.
evidence.support_span: with posts identifying the location as Texas in the US.

evidence.statement: A Reddit post features the same footage and identifies the location as Texas.
An Instagram post from January 6, 2024, used the same video with a caption stating 1,000 crows swarmed a supermarket parking lot in Texas.
evidence.support_span: another Instagram post from January 6, 2024, carrying the same video. The video was uploaded with the caption, "1,000 crows swarms a Supermarket parking lot in Texas"

evidence.statement: The birds in the video are identified as great-tailed grackles, which are common in human-inhabited areas in the Houston area of Texas.
evidence.support_span: The report added that the blackbirds, known as great-tailed grackles, are commonly found in human-inhabited areas with trees and are especially widespread in the Houston area in Texas.
